title: The false-wake budget: per-window false-positive bound
caption: An always-on detector budgets one expected false wake per month. With ~1 non-keyword classification window per second, W_month is ~2.59M windows — so each window may false-fire at most ~4 times in ten million. Expected values add across correlated windows, so the bound holds even though neighboring windows aren't independent.

symbols.name: per-window false-positive rate
symbols.meaning: probability a single non-keyword window triggers a wake

symbols.name: false-wake budget
symbols.meaning: expected false wakes allowed per month (here: 1)

symbols.name: windows per month
symbols.meaning: non-keyword classification windows evaluated monthly (~2.59M at 1/s)

title: Rule of three: evidence for a zero-event claim
caption: If zero events are observed in n independent trials, the one-sided ~95% upper bound on the true rate is about 3/n. Claiming one false wake per month therefore needs ~3 months of representative listening with zero observed wakes — fewer hours establishes a weaker claim, not a pass.

symbols.name: rate upper bound
symbols.meaning: ~95% one-sided upper bound on the true event rate after zero observations

symbols.name: trials observed
symbols.meaning: independent windows / listening units with zero events

symbols.name: required listening duration
symbols.meaning: representative audio needed before a rate claim can be accepted

symbols.name: target event rate
symbols.meaning: the rate being claimed (e.g. 1 false wake per month)

title: Cohen's kappa: chance-corrected annotator agreement
caption: Raw agreement lies on skewed classes: two annotators agreeing 90% on a 90/10 class split agree mostly by chance. Kappa discounts the expected chance agreement, so label quality is judged against what guessing would already score.

symbols.name: Cohen's kappa
symbols.meaning: agreement beyond chance; 1 = perfect, 0 = chance-level, <0 = worse than chance

symbols.name: observed agreement
symbols.meaning: fraction of items both annotators labeled identically

symbols.name: expected agreement
symbols.meaning: agreement expected if each annotator labeled independently at their own class rates

title: Predictive entropy: a supervision-quality signal
caption: Entropy of a trained model's predictive distribution. Inconsistent labels train the model to spread probability across competing classes, so rising entropy flags supervision problems — trustworthy only if the model is calibrated, and ambiguous with hard inputs, shift, or calibration drift as alternative causes.

symbols.name: predictive entropy
symbols.meaning: spread of the model's predicted class distribution; rises on contradictory supervision

symbols.name: predicted class probability
symbols.meaning: model probability assigned to class i for a given input

title: Population Stability Index: binned-distribution drift
caption: Bins a feature by the baseline distribution (typically deciles) and scores how the current distribution reweights each bin. Conventional bands: <0.1 stable, 0.1–0.25 moderate shift, >0.25 investigate — conventions to calibrate per deployment, not physical limits.

symbols.name: actual share
symbols.meaning: fraction of current/production observations falling in bin i

symbols.name: expected share
symbols.meaning: fraction of baseline/training observations falling in bin i

symbols.name: population stability index
symbols.meaning: single divergence score for a binned feature; larger = more reweighting vs baseline

title: Kolmogorov–Smirnov: max-gap drift statistic
latex: D_{KS} = \max_x \lvert F_P(x) - F_Q(x) \rvert, \qquad D_{crit} \approx 1.36\sqrt{\frac{n_P + n_Q}{n_P n_Q}}
caption: Nonparametric: compares the empirical CDFs of a baseline batch P and a current batch Q without assuming a distribution family. Exceeding the critical distance at a chosen significance level is an investigation trigger for a univariate continuous feature — not a universal failure rule.

symbols.name: K-S statistic
symbols.meaning: largest vertical gap between the two empirical CDFs

symbols.name: empirical CDFs
symbols.meaning: cumulative distributions of the baseline (P) and current (Q) samples

symbols.name: critical distance
symbols.meaning: threshold at ~5% significance; shrinks as either sample grows

symbols.name: sample sizes
symbols.meaning: observation counts in the two compared batches

title: The feeding bound: min of compute and supply
caption: Step time is set by the slower of compute and input — feeding loss is the idle fraction when IO wins. The supply rate is physical bandwidth discounted by format efficiency (columnar vs row parsing) and loader/decode overhead; every discount is a stage in the input path.

symbols.name: step time
symbols.meaning: wall-clock duration of one training step

symbols.name: input time
symbols.meaning: time to read, decode, transform, and transfer one step's batch

symbols.name: data supply rate
symbols.meaning: usable bytes/samples the input path delivers per second

symbols.name: format efficiency
symbols.meaning: fraction of physical bandwidth surviving the container format (Parquet columnar >> CSV/JSON row parse)

symbols.name: pipeline overhead
symbols.meaning: fraction lost to decode, transform, and transfer work in the loader path

title: Data debt compounding
caption: Debt measured as the engineer-hours needed to bring every debt metric below its warning threshold, growing at a net rate r per planning period. A planning heuristic, not a physical law — real backlogs jump at discrete upstream migrations, and pseudo-label loops make debt compound into dependent systems.

symbols.name: debt after n periods
symbols.meaning: projected remediation backlog in engineer-hours

symbols.name: current debt
symbols.meaning: today's remediation backlog — hours to clear all warning thresholds

symbols.name: net growth rate
symbols.meaning: fraction the backlog grows per planning period, net of remediation

symbols.name: elapsed periods
symbols.meaning: planning periods since the Debt_0 measurement
